models.mechanism: The new verse gives the emergence model a full temporal passage: darkness enters and conceals, the dependent seeker remains close to a nurturing Lord through that vulnerable interval, and الفلق names the eventual splitting-open into light and manifestation. Refuge is therefore not escape from every hidden phase; it is guarded continuity through concealment until safe emergence.

structural_cues: ٱلْفَلَقِ in 113:1 and غَاسِقٍ إِذَا وَقَبَ in 113:3 form a direct light/dark and opening/entering reversal.
إِذَا marks a phase transition: danger is specified when darkness enters rather than as an undifferentiated permanent state.
113:2's خَلَقَ keeps the stage-1 creation/emergence bridge active between the two temporal poles.
The sequence refuge → Lord of opening → created field → darkness entering supports a backward-looking request to be carried from concealment toward opening.

abductive_moves.assumption: The entering darkness is a vulnerable hidden phase in the same process that ends with الفلق, not merely an unrelated nocturnal threat.
abductive_moves.why_invoked: The packet gives temporal opposition and adjacent sequence but does not explicitly state a single cycle.
abductive_moves.causal_direction: darkness enters → vulnerable concealment persists → daybreak splits it open
alternatives: 113:3 names only an external night danger
الفلق is creation generally rather than the endpoint of darkness

abductive_moves.assumption: Lordly nurture can make concealment guarded without making the threatening darkness itself beneficial.
abductive_moves.why_invoked: The packet supplies nurture, darkness, evil, and emergence but not the distinction between protected hiddenness and harmful concealment.
abductive_moves.causal_direction: stage-by-stage care during concealment → preserved life → safe emergence
alternatives: refuge means immediate removal from darkness

changed_reading.before: The focus sought caregiver-like protection from harmful potentials encountered as creation emerges.
changed_reading.after: It now asks for sustained nurture through a timed dark/concealed phase until creation can be safely split open into light and manifestation.

models.ablation: Removing 113:3 غ س ق/و ق ب collapses the newly activated hidden interval and returns the model to generic protected emergence; removing ف ل ق B002-B003 removes its terminal opening; removing ع و ذ/rabb nurture branches leaves a day-night cycle without guarded continuity.

models.mechanism: The threshold model becomes one of controlled permeability. الفلق can be an opening or low cleft; خ ل ق can name a water-holding hollow or an imperforate closure; و ق ب is a receiving recess or aperture; and غ س ق can pour like liquid. The Lord of الفلق is thus read as governor of openings and receptacles, while refuge asks that harmful influx not penetrate the seeker's vulnerable interior and that a safe outlet still be opened.

models.mechanism: The speech model is redirected from countering fabrication to maintaining orientation when visibility collapses. قُلْ requires audible articulation; غ س ق can darken the eye; و ق ب describes entry into concealment; and الفلق supplies clarification after obscurity. The protective utterance becomes an alternative channel of indication when sight no longer guides, keeping the speaker directed toward the Lord of disclosure until light returns.

models.mechanism: Refuge is newly read as interruption rather than total prevention. ع و ذ can describe escaping after fright or even after an intended killing blow fails to complete; 113:3 marks danger precisely when darkness enters; and الفلق supplies the later reversal that breaks the interval open. The focus asks the Lord to preserve the seeker after threat has begun but before its harmful intention reaches completion.

structural_cues: إِذَا marks danger conditionally at the moment of entry, distinguishing onset from completion.
The repeated مِن شَرِّ names a harmful outcome while ع و ذ B006 lexically supplies an attempt that does not reach its intended result.
الفلق and darkness-entering form endpoints of a temporal interval: closing/entry followed by splitting/open.
The refuge verb precedes the threat sequence, framing it as a request that can govern what happens after onset.

abductive_moves.assumption: إِذَا وَقَبَ marks the beginning of a harmful process whose completion remains preventable.
abductive_moves.why_invoked: The packet states when darkness enters and calls its evil a refuge-source, but it does not describe an attack sequence.
abductive_moves.causal_direction: darkness enters → harmful process begins → possible completion
alternatives: the danger is fully present at entry

abductive_moves.assumption: The Lord of daybreak interrupts the sequence so that onset does not become completed injury.
abductive_moves.why_invoked: ع و ذ B006 supplies failed completion and ف ل ق B002 supplies reversal, but the protective causal arrow is inferred.
abductive_moves.causal_direction: refuge with Lord of daybreak → interruption before completion → survival
alternatives: daybreak follows temporally but does not cause preservation

changed_reading.before: The focus generally requested protection from harmful capacities in creation.
changed_reading.after: It specifically allows that danger may enter and fear or contact may occur, while asking that the sequence be broken before intended harm is completed.

models.ablation: Removing 113:3 إِذَا وَقَبَ removes the onset event and collapses the model to generic refuge; removing ع و ذ B006 removes the failed-completion structure; removing ف ل ق B002 removes the reversal that terminates the interval.

surprise_reading: 113:3 makes the focus a passage through entry and reversal. It can mean nurture through a dark concealed phase until safe emergence; governance of a porous threshold so harmful influx cannot penetrate; an audible compass when the eye loses light; or preservation after threat begins so that its intended harm never reaches completion.
discarded_or_unchanged: The stage-1 false-speech/fabrication submechanism receives no new bridge from 113:3 and is not repeated independently.
